intro: You are standing in a frontier town of soldiers. This is Zerzevan Castle, in Diyarbakır province, from the 3rd century AD: a Roman garrison town on the Persian frontier. Below it lies a rock-cut Mithraeum, the best preserved temple of that cult known in Anatolia.
history: The Roman garrison town on the Persian frontier was founded in the third century AD and stayed in use into the seventh. Much of it still survives: its wall, watchtower, church, cisterns and underground shelters. And beneath it all is the rock-cut Mithraeum, the best preserved temple of that soldiers' cult known in Anatolia.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Mithraeum and the watchtower. Then seek out the underground shelter, and end at the church.
facts: Did you know? The cult of Mithras spread through the Roman army, and its temples were deliberately built dark and cave-like. At Zerzevan that rule is cut straight into the rock. This rock-cut Mithraeum is the best preserved temple of that soldiers' cult known in Anatolia. The town itself was a Roman garrison on the Persian frontier, and it stayed in use for four centuries.
outro: This brings our tour of Zerzevan Castle to an end. Please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. These walls once guarded a frontier; now let us guard them for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
